History of Morocco.fact: Idris' loyal Arab ex-slave and companion Rashid brought up the boy and took on himself the regency of the state, on behalf of the Awraba. In 801 Rashid was killed by the Abbasids.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: Under his son and successor Muhammad (828–836) the kingdom was divided amongst seven of his brothers, whereby eight Idrisid statelets formed in Morocco and western Algeria. Muhammad himself came to rule Fes, with only nominal power over his brothers.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Muhammad entrusted his brother _____, who had received the territories around the Rif, to punish Isa
History of Morocco.fact: Muhammad entrusted his brother Umar, who had received the territories around the Rif, to punish Isa. Umar successfully drove Isa from power, who was forced to take refuge in Chellah, and then turned north to punish his other brother al-Qasim at Tangier because he had earlier refused to join him and Muhammad against Isa.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Al-Qasim fled to _____ and settled nearby, while Muhammad gave Umar governorship of Tangier as a reward
History of Morocco.fact: Al-Qasim fled to Asilah and settled nearby, while Muhammad gave Umar governorship of Tangier as a reward.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: Muhammad himself died seven months later in the March or April 836.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: After his death in 849 he was succeeded by his brother Yahya ibn _____ (or Yahya I), who also enjoyed a peaceful reign
History of Morocco.fact: Muhammad himself died seven months later in the March or April 836. His son Ali ibn Muhammad inherited his position and ruled for 13 years (836–849) in a competent manner, ensuring the stability of the state.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: During this time Islamic and Arabic culture gained a stronghold in the towns and Morocco profited from the trans-Saharan trade, which came to be dominated by Muslim (mostly Berber) traders. Even so, the Islamic and Arabic culture only made its influence felt in the towns, with the vast majority of Morocco's population still using the Berber languages and often adhering to Islamic heterodox and heretical doctrines.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: After an episode of disorder in Fes his cousin Ali ibn Umar took over power. From their base in Sefrou they were able to defeat Ali ibn Umar and occupy Fes.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: In 868, under the leadership of the Abd al-Razzaq the _____ tribes of Madyuna, Ghayata and Miknasa of the Fes region formed a common front against the Idrisids

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: From their base in Sefrou they were able to defeat Ali ibn Umar and occupy Fes.

History of Morocco.fact: Fes refused to submit, however, and another Yahya, the son of al-Qasim, was able to retake the city and establish himself as the new ruler, Yahya III. Yahya III ruled over the entire Idrisid realm and continued to attack the Sufris.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: Fes refused to submit, however, and another Yahya, the son of al-Qasim, was able to retake the city and establish himself as the new ruler, Yahya III. Yahya III ruled over the entire Idrisid realm and continued to attack the Sufris.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: Thus the ruling line had passed from the sons of Muhammad to the son of Umar and now the sons of al-Qasim.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Yahya III ruled over the entire _____ realm and continued to attack the Sufris
History of Morocco.fact: Yahya III ruled over the entire Idrisid realm and continued to attack the Sufris.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: In 917 the Miknasa and its leader Masala ibn Habus, acting on behalf of their Fatimid allies, attacked Fes and forced Yahya IV to recognize Fatimid suzerainty, before deposing him in 919 or 921. From Fes, the Miknasa began pursuing the Idrisid family across Morocco.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: He was succeeded by his cousin _____ ibn Abul 'Afiya, who had already been given charge over the rest of the country
History of Morocco.fact: He was succeeded by his cousin Musa ibn Abul 'Afiya, who had already been given charge over the rest of the country. The Idrisid Hassan I al-Hajam, a grandson of al-Qasim, managed to wrest control of Fez from 925 but in 927 Musa returned, captured Hassan and killed him, marking the last time the Idrisids held power in Fes.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco, where the _____ besieged them
History of Morocco.fact: From Fes, the Miknasa began pursuing the Idrisid family across Morocco. The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco, where the Miknasa besieged them.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
